primitive.relation: Directed neighbourhoods of a finite digraph (diGraphType D) and the in-degree and regularity predicates read through them. Canonical bodies: Digraph.foundations.neighbourhoods.Nout v := [set w | v --> w], Nin v := [set u | u --> v] and Nout2 v := [set w | [&& w != v, w \notin Nout v & [exists u, (u \in Nout v) && (u --> w)]]] (directed distance exactly two; both exclusions kept); the in-degree is B16's Digraph.foundations.degree_balance.indeg v := #|[set u | u --> v]| (#|Nin v| by conversion), beside core oriented.outdeg; d-diregularity is degree_balance.diregular d := [forall v : D, (outdeg v == d) && (indeg v == d)] (Boolean, out-degree conjunct first). classic_core Nout/Nin/Nout2/indeg/diregular and colouring_variants.indeg are transparent aliases of these bodies (conversion; names, declared types, implicit arguments and transparency unchanged). Loops count on both sides, digons are allowed, and diregularity is vacuous on the empty carrier for every d. STAGED (master-directed-neighbourhood-scope-decision.md 6d6d2b8d, option C): core/tournament's N_out/N_in (the same comprehensions restricted to a tournament), the three rows that reach this family only through them (X2 tournament_outneighborhood_degeneracy_statement and tournament_outneighborhood_cycle_statement, X93 local_tournament_dichromatic_bound_statement) and the X93 chain x93_t_local_tournament are a LATER STAGE of this family: the migration tools admit no public source under core/ (family_registry.public_repository_path), so they need a gate-tooling change admitting core/ or another reviewed route. They are untouched here (core/tournament.v keeps its parent text); the measured N_in ascription finding is kept for that stage.

digraph-neighbourhood.note: classic_core Nout v := [set w | v --> w], Nin v := [set u | u --> v] and Nout2 (distance exactly two: w != v, w \notin Nout v and a common out-neighbour) are the neighbourhoods bodies verbatim; the aliases keep their {set D} declared types and the Section's implicit D.

in-degree.note: classic_core.indeg v := #|Nin v| and colouring_variants.indeg D v := #|[set u | u --> v]| are B16's degree_balance.indeg v by conversion; colouring_variants.indeg keeps its explicit D and has no live consumer.

diregular.note: classic_core.diregular d := [forall v, (outdeg v == d) && (indeg v == d)] is degree_balance.diregular D d by conversion (diregular_compat); diregular_ascription records the unchanged declared type; vacuous on the empty carrier, a loop counts once on each side.

legacy-axiom-defect.note: reals_growth.indeg D v := #|[set w : D | w --> v]| has the canonical in-degree body but is NOT migrated here, for the reason B16 records for reals_growth.eulerian, its only consumer: the two non-corpus EC-log rows inherit four classical-reals axioms through their statements, so a certificate of them fails the kernel assumptions audit. upstream_audit.note: coq-graph-theory has open_neigh u := [set v | u -- v] (N(u)) and closed_neigh on its diGraph record, but no in-neighbourhood, no second neighbourhood and no in- or out-degree (B16's audit). Digraph's HB carrier reaches it only through to_GT D := RelType (@arc D), a Definition, not a coercion; open_neigh (to_GT D) u = Nout u is a bridge, never a canonical body. The Digraph core has outdeg (core/oriented.v) and B16 owns indeg; this family adds the focused public neighbourhoods module (prelude and core/digraph only) and degree_balance.diregular, and aliases the conjecture-local copies.
